info.title: UnQ API
info.summary: Order and pay at the table, split the bill, run the shop.
info.description:
The API behind UnQ, a food and drinks ordering app: diners at a venue scan their table's QR code, order from their phones, pick what each of them pays for, and pay by PayPal or card (Stripe); managers run their shops, menus and tables from the same app.

## Conventions

- **Sign-in** is two HttpOnly cookies, `accessToken` (15 minutes) and `refreshToken` (4 weeks), set by the auth routes. Each sign-in is a session of its own, so an account can be signed in on several devices (up to 10) and sign one out (`DELETE /auth/sessions/{sessionId}`). A 401 means refresh (`POST /auth/refreshToken`) and retry; a refresh that fails ends the session. Operations marked with the lock need the cookie; the rest are public, and some show more to a signed-in caller.
- **Roles.** Every account is a `customer`; a `shopMg` (shop manager) can create shops, and an `admin` can do everything on every shop. Never from the account's own request (register, profile edit): an administrator gives them (the Accounts operations), and the first administrator is set in the database. A shop's staff are its `members`, each with a role (`owner`, one per shop, or `manager`), added by the owner (the Staff operations); the owner, or an administrator, alone adds managers, removes other members and hands the shop over, and any member may leave; manager routes check that the caller is a member of the shop in the URL, or an administrator (403 otherwise).
- **Ids** are MongoDB ObjectIds (24 hex characters). A table's id is its `_id` in the shop's `tables`.
- **Money** is in pounds (GBP) to the penny everywhere a cart, a payment or a refund says an amount, and the `price` a manager sets is the same. The one exception is `createStripeCheckout`'s `amount`, in pence, as Stripe counts. The client never names an amount to pay: every total comes from database prices.
- **Errors** are `{ message, details?, reason? }`. `400 Validation failed` carries `details`, one `{ path, message }` per problem; a few errors carry a machine-readable `reason`. A 5xx says only "Generic Server Error" unless its message was written for the user.
- **Rate limits**, per account, not per IP: wrong passwords (10 in 15 minutes, wherever tried), a diner's cart changes (120 a minute, starting a card payment included; capturing a payment is never limited) and people added (20 an hour, an account created or attached by an administrator or a shop's staff). All configurable (`PASSWORD_FAILS_PER_ACCOUNT`, `CART_EDITS_PER_MINUTE`, `PEOPLE_ADDED_PER_HOUR`).
- **Soft deletes.** A deleted menu item stays, unavailable, for the carts that hold it; a deleted table stays under the shop's `deletedTables` so its carts and money stay reachable; a shop is deleted for good, with everything in it, once no money is moving.
- **Concurrency.** A cart is saved under optimistic concurrency: a write that meets a newer version retries or answers 409 "The cart changed, please retry".

## Checkout

A diner selects units to pay for (`addSplitItem`), then pays in two calls around the provider's UI: PayPal `createCheckoutOrder` → popup → `captureCheckout`; card `createStripeCheckout` → Payment Element → `captureStripeCheckout`. The second call re-checks everything before money moves, and a payment that can't be recorded afterwards is refunded automatically. A card payment the diner abandons after authorising is still finished by Stripe's webhook or the server's 2-minute sweep, and the diner is told the outcome in their cart's `notices` on their next visit.

post.summary: Create an account and sign in
post.description: A new account with the customer role; the shopMg and admin roles are given by an administrator (POST /users, PUT /users/{userId}/role), the first administrator in the database. Sets the `accessToken` (15 minutes) and `refreshToken` (4 weeks) cookies: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=None. The sign-in is a session of its own on the account (a device), beside the ones other devices hold: at most 10, the oldest sign-in going beyond that. The avatar is a generated initials image.

email.description: Trimmed and lowercased before it's checked and stored

400.description: "Validation failed" (details), or the model's own validation message

409.description: "Email already registered"

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description: Sets the `accessToken` (15 minutes) and `refreshToken` (4 weeks) cookies: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=None. The sign-in is a session of its own on the account (a device), beside the ones other devices hold: at most 10, the oldest sign-in going beyond that. Wrong passwords count towards the account's limit (lib/passwordLimit.ts); an email with no account, or a Google-only account, doesn't.

401.description: "Invalid credentials": no such account, no password on it, or the wrong password

post.summary: Rotate the session's tokens
post.description: Reads the `refreshToken` cookie. A valid one that is its session's current token is swapped atomically for a new pair (both cookies set again). One its session replaced in the last minute answers 401 with `reason: "superseded"` and leaves the cookies alone: another tab of the same device just refreshed, and the request can be resent with the cookies that tab got. Any other invalid one (expired, replaced earlier, signed with another key, account gone, session gone: a logout, a revocation, a password change, a sign-in on too many devices) answers 401 and clears both cookies: the session is over.

400.description: "Refresh token MUST be provided!": no cookie

401.description: "Invalid token", with `reason: "superseded"` when another tab just rotated it (cookies kept); without it the cookies are cleared

get.description: Ends this device's session and clears both cookies. The account's other devices stay signed in.
The account's sessions in sign-in order, the caller's marked `current`. A device that hasn't refreshed in four weeks holds an expired token and isn't listed. Never the tokens or their ids.

delete.description: Ends that session: its next refresh fails, so the device is a guest's within 15 minutes (the access token's life). Revoking the caller's own session also clears the cookies, like a logout.

204.description: Signed out; cookies cleared when it was this device's

404.description: "Session not found": not one of the account's sessions (or "User not found!")

get.description: Redirects the browser to Google (scopes profile and email). Open it as a navigation, not an XHR.

Where Google sends the browser back (its callback URL is `PUBLIC_API_URL/auth/googleRedirect`). An account already linked by Google id signs in; otherwise an account with the same verified email is linked (its password is removed: only Google signs it in from now on); a new email gets a new account. An unverified email that matches an account, or no email, signs nobody in. Sets the cookies and redirects to the front end's origin (`FRONTEND_URL`, else `FRONTEND_DEV_URL`); a sign-in that can't be matched safely redirects to its `/login` page instead. On a dev server with no front end running, that last redirect fails to connect; the cookies are set all the same (check with GET /users/me from /docs).

302.description: To the front end, signed in; or to its /login page, not signed in

get.description: Newest first, each with the shops it is a member of and its role on each. `q` matches the name, surname or email, case aside. An empty parameter counts as absent.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text to search for (up to 100 characters); empty or absent lists every account

409.description: "Email already registered"

409.description: "Transfer or delete their shops first": the account owns a shop

post.summary: Create a shop
post.description: The caller becomes its owner (`ownerId`, the first of its `members`). An administrator is never a member, so one names the owner instead (`ownerId`, any account but another administrator's); from anyone else the field is refused.

phone.description: As typed, up to 30 characters: digits, spaces, dashes, brackets, +

timeZone.description: An IANA time zone name (Europe/London, America/New_York): the zone the shop's days are counted in; Europe/London unless set

ownerId.description: Administrators only: the account that owns the new shop

400.description: "Validation failed" (details); "Name the shop's owner (ownerId): an administrator isn't a member"

403.description: "Shop Manager Only!!": the account can't create shops; "Only an administrator names an owner": `ownerId` from a shop manager

404.description: "User not found!": the token's account no longer exists; "Owner not found": no account has the `ownerId`

409.description: "An administrator can't be a member of a shop": the `ownerId` is an administrator's

get.description: Menus populated, deleted tables left out. The home page uses `GET /shops/browse` instead.

The shops the caller is a member of, whatever their account role: `[]` for an account on none, every shop for an administrator. Menus populated. Each deleted table says whether something there still needs the staff (`needsAttention`) and until when its closed carts stay on its sheet (`recentCartsUntil`). A shop from before membership gets its `ownerId` and `members` here, from its `shopMg`.

200.description: The shops the caller is a member of

get.description: Oldest first, by id. With `q`, only shops whose name or bio holds it, or whose menu has an item named with it (case aside). `next` is the cursor for the page after, null on the last. An empty parameter counts as absent; a repeated one fails.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Text to search for (up to 100 characters); empty or absent lists every shop

get.description: Menu populated, deleted tables left out.

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"

put.description: Any member of the shop, whatever their account role (or an administrator). Every field optional; only the ones sent change. An empty `phone` clears it.

phone.description: As typed, up to 30 characters: digits, spaces, dashes, brackets, +

timeZone.description: An IANA time zone name (Europe/London, America/New_York): the zone the shop's days are counted in

200.description: The shop as it is now (menu by id)

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"; "User not found!"

delete.summary: Delete a shop and everything in it
delete.description: The owner's alone (or an administrator's). Takes its menu items (deleted ones too), its carts (payment records included) and its pay-backs; the orders remain as the sales record, written first (nothing is deleted if they can't be). Refused while money is still moving: an open cart, a payment or refund a provider hasn't confirmed, a card payment still being finished, a diner to pay back, or a payment that can still be refunded from a table's sheet (a paid cart closed or changed in the last 24 hours).

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"; "User not found!"

409.description: "A table in this shop has an open cart — close it first"; "A payment or refund at table … is still awaiting PayPal|Stripe — check it there first"; "A payment at table … can still be refunded from its sheet: the shop can be deleted once no paid cart has changed for a day"; or a card-payment reason (carts/stripeDeletion.ts)

500.description: "The shop's sales records couldn't be saved, so nothing was deleted. Try again shortly."; or "Generic Server Error"

get.description: Each joined to their account (name, email, avatar), the owner first. Any member of the shop, or an administrator.

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"; "User not found!"

post.summary: Add someone to the shop
post.description: By their email. An address with an account attaches that account, name and password untouched (200); one without gets an account created from `name`, `surname` and `password`, which the caller tells them (201; account role `customer`, `createdBy` the caller). Only the owner (or an administrator) adds a `manager`. One update puts them in both membership lists, so two adds of one person land once. Counts towards the caller's people-added limit, created or attached.

password.description: For a new account: at least 8 characters, its first password

201.description: An account created for them, attached

400.description: "Validation failed" (details; for a new account, name, surname and password are "Required for a new account"); "That is your own address"

403.description: "Shop Manager Only!": not a member of this shop; "Only the owner adds managers"

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"; "User not found!"

409.description: "Already a member"; "An administrator can't be a member of a shop"; "The shop's staff changed, please retry": the shop lost its owner or the account went in the same instant

delete.description: The owner (or an administrator) removes anyone but the owner; a manager only the roles below manager (none yet); any member themselves (leaving). The owner is never removed: the shop is handed over first. The account stays.

403.description: "Shop Manager Only!": not a member of this shop; "The owner can't be removed"; "Only the owner removes a manager"

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"; "Not a member of this shop"; "User not found!"

409.description: "The shop's staff changed, please retry": a hand-over landed in the same instant

put.description: The owner (or an administrator) names a member, who becomes the owner; the previous owner becomes a manager. One update, matched on the current owner.

200.description: The members, as GET /shops/{shopId}/staff lists them

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"; "Not a member of this shop"; "User not found!"

409.description: "Already the owner"; "The shop's staff changed, please retry": another hand-over, a removal or a deletion landed in the same instant

put.description: The manager check runs before the upload, so a refused request never reaches Cloudinary. The replaced image is deleted there if this app uploaded it.

cover.description: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF or HEIC, at most 5 MB

200.description: The shop with its new cover (menu by id)

400.description: "Only JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF or HEIC images can be uploaded"; "No image was sent (field \"cover\")"

post.summary: Add a table
post.description: Names are unique within the shop (checked in the same update, so two requests at once can't both pass). The table's QR URL is its page in the front end.

get.description: Any signed-in user. Deleted tables are not listed.

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"; "User not found!"

get.description: What the table's QR code opens. A deleted table, or another shop's, is not found.

404.description: "Table Not Found!": no such shop, or no such table in it

put.description: The new name must be unique within the shop. Answers the shop's whole table list, not the one table.

200.description: All the shop's tables, with the rename

404.description: "Table Not Found!"; "Shop Not Found!"

delete.description: Moved to the shop's deleted tables rather than dropped: it takes no orders and diners don't see it, but the manager can still open its recent carts to refund them. Refused while it has an open cart (close it first) or a payment or refund awaiting its provider. Deleting it twice is a 204 both times.

404.description: "Table Not Found!"; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "This table has an open cart — close it first"; "A payment or refund at this table is still awaiting PayPal|Stripe — check it first"; "The table changed, please try again"

get.summary: The shop's sales over a range of days
get.description: Everything the sales page shows, in one answer: totals, a zero-filled series by day, week or month, sales by weekday and hour, items by revenue, refunds by reason and hour, and the tables. Counted as a till would, in the shop's time zone: gross is completed payments by the day paid; refunds count on the day they were made (completed only), whenever their sale was; net is the difference. Visits are distinct carts, diners distinct payers, and a returning diner had paid at this shop before the range began. Items are net of refunded units under the name and price diners saw last. With `compare=previous`, the range of the same length ending the day before is reported too. At most 366 days.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first day, YYYY-MM-DD, in the shop's time zone

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last day, included; with `from`, a range of at most 366 days (so at most 365 days after it)

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: How the series is bucketed; unless given, by day up to 92 days and by week beyond. Weeks start on Monday

parameters.name: compare
parameters.description: `previous` adds the range of the same length ending the day before `from`

get.summary: One of the report's tables as a CSV file
get.description: Counted as the report counts, in the shop's time zone, as a download. `orders`: a row per payment made in the range, completed or still pending (paid at, table, provider, status, amount, refunded to date, net, items as "2× Latte, 1× Sea Bass"); `items`: a row per menu item sold, by revenue; `days`: a row per day of the range, zero-filled, with the category and provider splits. No diner is named or identified in any of them. UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, CRLF line ends; a cell that would start with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@` or a tab gets a leading apostrophe so a spreadsheet can't run it as a formula.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first day, YYYY-MM-DD, in the shop's time zone

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last day, included; with `from`, a range of at most 366 days (so at most 365 days after it)

Content-Disposition.description: attachment; filename=<shop>-sales-<from>-<to>-<table>.csv (the shop's name as letters, digits and dashes)

get.summary: Every table's state at a glance
get.description: One entry per current table, from its open cart(s): what's owed and paid, who's waiting, and what needs attention (a sold-out item ordered, two open carts, a selection held over 15 minutes, a payment the provider hasn't confirmed, a diner to pay back).

The open cart(s), those closed in the last 24 hours (or older but still awaiting a provider), and the table's pay-backs. Payment and refund records and the manager log included; diners by first name only. Works for a deleted table too.

404.description: "Table Not Found!": not a current or deleted table of this shop; "Shop Not Found!"

post.summary: Free units diners hold in open selections
post.description: Everyone's (empty body), one diner's (`userId`), the selections of diners whose account no longer exists (`userId: null`), or one item's (`menuId`), so others can pay for them. Each diner affected gets a note; the manager log gets a line. No money moves.

userId.description: One diner's selections; null: those of diners whose account is gone; absent: everyone's

404.description: "Cart Not Found!"; "No selection to release"; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "The cart changed, please retry": another write landed first (a payment settling, another manager)

post.summary: Take an item's unpaid units out of the cart
post.description: All of them, diners' selections of it included (the diner's own bin leaves others' selections); paid units stay as the record. A cart left with nothing ordered and nothing paid closes, so the table is free again. The table's diners get a note.

404.description: "Cart Not Found!"; "Item Not Found in Cart!"; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "Nothing unpaid to remove"; "The cart changed, please retry": another write landed first (a payment settling, another manager)

post.summary: Close the table's cart
post.description: Unpaid units and open selections are dropped (the kitchen only acts on paid orders); paid units stay. A cart where nothing was ever paid is deleted instead. Refused while a payment on it awaits its provider.

200.description: What happened: deleted, or closed with the cart

404.description: "Cart Not Found!": no open cart with this id at this table of this shop; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "A payment on this table is still awaiting PayPal|Stripe: check it first"; "The cart changed, please retry": another write landed first (a payment settling, another manager)

post.summary: Merge a duplicate open cart into the newest one
post.description: For a table with more than one open cart (data from before the one-open-cart index). Moves this older cart's unpaid units and open selections into the newest cart, the one diners see; its paid units stay on it as the record and it closes (or is deleted if nothing on it was ever paid). Answers the newest cart.

404.description: "Cart Not Found!": no open cart with this id at this table of this shop; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "This table has only one open cart"; "Merge the older cart into the newest one"; "A payment on this table is still awaiting PayPal|Stripe: check it first"; "The cart changed, please retry": another write landed first (a payment settling, another manager)

post.summary: Refund units of one payment
post.description: At the prices that payment charged; the units leave the cart (cancelled, not made payable again). Open or closed carts of the shop. A `pending` refund record is saved first (so a double click can't refund twice), the provider is asked with the record's id as its idempotency key, then the record is completed or marked failed. If the provider's answer is unclear the record stays pending: retry it. The payer gets a note; a pay-back is opened if Stripe later fails the refund.

lines.description: Units to refund, each item once

reasonNote.description: What happened, 1 to 200 characters: required with "other", refused otherwise

200.description: The completed refund and the cart

400.description: "Validation failed" (details, whose messages include "List each item once", "Say what happened" and "A note goes with the reason Other only"); "That item isn't in this payment"; "Only N× … of this payment can still be refunded"; "… from this payment has already been refunded"

404.description: "Cart Not Found!": not a cart of this shop; "Payment Not Found!"; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "PayPal|Stripe hasn't confirmed this payment yet: check it first"; "This payment didn't go through at PayPal|Stripe: nothing was taken"; "This payment can only be refunded from PayPal|Stripe" (no capture or charge id); "The cart changed, please retry": another write landed first (a payment settling, another manager)

500.description: "The refund went through at PayPal|Stripe but couldn't be recorded here. It shows as in progress: retry it to record it."; or "Generic Server Error"

502.description: "PayPal|Stripe didn't confirm the refund (…). It shows as in progress: retry it, which checks with PayPal|Stripe first." (outcome unknown; the record stays pending); "…. Nothing was refunded." (refused; the record is marked failed)

post.summary: Settle a refund left in progress
post.description: Asks the provider whether it has the refund (by the record's id). If so, it's recorded as the provider says (completed, or failed); if not, it's sent again under the same id, which the provider can't apply twice.

404.description: "Cart Not Found!"; "Refund Not Found!"; "Payment Not Found!"; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "This refund isn't in progress any more"

500.description: "The refund went through at PayPal|Stripe but couldn't be recorded here. …"; or "Generic Server Error"

502.description: "Couldn't check with PayPal|Stripe (…). The refund is still in progress: try again shortly."; "PayPal|Stripe says this refund failed. Nothing was refunded."; or the messages of POST …/refunds

post.summary: Ask the provider about a pending payment
post.description: For a payment the provider hadn't confirmed at checkout (`status: pending`). Confirmed: it becomes `completed`, and the cart closes if that was all it waited for. Failed: it becomes `failed`, its units are unpaid again and back in the payer's selection (the cart reopens if it had closed). Still pending: nothing changes. The payer is told either way.

200.description: The payment as it is now, and the cart

404.description: "Cart Not Found!"; "Payment Not Found!"; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "This payment isn't awaiting confirmation any more"; "PayPal|Stripe is still processing this payment. Check again later"; "The cart changed, please retry": another write landed first (a payment settling, another manager)

502.description: "Couldn't check with PayPal|Stripe (…). Try again shortly."

post.summary: Mark a pay-back done
post.description: `as` must be what the sheet showed: `paidBack` (staff gave the diner the money another way), `handled` (a disputed payment: the bank returns it), or `checked` (a hand-over whose payment a cart now shows as paid). One already done answers as it was marked, whatever was asked. One that changed since the sheet showed it is refused, so what's stored is what the manager confirmed. The cart gets a log line without touching its `updatedAt`.

as.description: What the sheet showed for this pay-back

200.description: The pay-back as it is now

404.description: "Pay-back Not Found!": not this shop's, or gone with it; "Shop Not Found!"

409.description: "This pay-back changed: here it is again"

price.description: In pounds, to the penny (at most 2 decimals): refunds price each unit on its own

404.description: "Shop Not Found!"

price.description: In pounds, to the penny (at most 2 decimals): refunds price each unit on its own

available.description: Defaults to true. false marks the item sold out: it can't be added, selected or paid for, and stays flagged in carts that hold it

200.description: The item as it is now

404.description: "Menu Item Not Found!": no such item, or not on this shop's menu; "Shop Not Found!"

delete.description: The item leaves the shop's menu but is kept, unavailable and marked `deletedFrom`, so carts that hold it still name it (as sold out). It goes for good with the shop.

404.description: "Menu Item Not Found!": not on this shop's menu; "Shop Not Found!"

put.description: The permission checks run before the upload, so a refused request never reaches Cloudinary. The replaced image is deleted there if this app uploaded it.

image.description: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF or HEIC, at most 5 MB

400.description: "Only JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF or HEIC images can be uploaded"; "No image was sent (field …)"

post.summary: Add units of an item to the table's order
post.description: A table has one shared open cart: whoever orders first creates it (the caller becomes its `userId`), everyone else adds to it. The item must be on this shop's menu and not sold out, and the table one of the shop's. Racing another diner's first order is retried onto the cart that won.

post.summary: Take units off an item's line (the −)
post.description: Drops the line at 0. Never into units already paid for or held in someone's open selection. A cart emptied this way is deleted (204) unless it holds payment, refund or manager records; one left with everything paid closes.

post.summary: Remove an item's unpaid units (the bin)
post.description: What stays: the paid units (the record of what was paid) and the units other diners have selected to pay for, with their selections; a line with neither is dropped. The caller's own selection goes with the units. A sold-out or deleted item goes whoever selected it (nobody can pay for it): this is how it leaves a cart. Version-checked, so a payment settling at the same moment conflicts instead of being overwritten. A cart emptied with nothing to keep is deleted (204).

204.description: The cart was emptied and deleted

post.summary: Select more units of an item to pay for
post.description: Grows the caller's open selection of the item, or starts one. The units every diner's open selections already hold, plus the request, plus the paid units must fit in the line: checked and claimed in one atomic update, so two diners racing for the last unit can't both get it. No new claims on a sold-out item.

post.description: Takes one unit off the caller's open selection of the item, dropping the selection at 0.

404.description: "Item Not Found!": the caller has no open selection of that item on this cart; "User not found!"

post.summary: Un-select an item
post.description: Drops the caller's open selection of the item.

404.description: "Item Not Found!": the caller has no open selection of that item on this cart; "User not found!"

post.summary: PayPal, step 1: an order for the amount due
post.description: Creates the PayPal order for exactly what the caller's open selections cost at database prices, bound to this cart and payer. Nothing is charged or stored. The checks run before PayPal is called, so a doomed checkout never mints an order. Not rate limited.

200.description: The order to approve in the popup

post.summary: PayPal, step 2: capture the approved order
post.description: The money-moving call. Refuses a replayed order id, runs step 1's checks again, confirms with PayPal that the order is approved, was minted for this cart and payer and matches the amount still due, and only then captures. The settlement is saved under optimistic concurrency; if it can't be (a concurrent payer took the units) the buyer is refunded automatically and told so. A capture PayPal holds for review is recorded as a pending payment (202): its units are held, the cart stays open, and a manager checks it later. Not rate limited.

post.summary: Card, step 1: a PaymentIntent for the amount due
post.description: Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent (manual capture: the card is only authorised) for exactly what the caller's open selections cost, and a record of it the server's sweep can see. Rate limited like an edit: each call makes an intent. An intent nobody confirms holds nothing and is cancelled after an hour.

200.description: The intent for the Payment Element

404.description: "Cart Not Found!": no open cart with this id at this table; "No open split items to pay!"; "User not found!"; "This table is no longer at a shop"

post.summary: Card, step 2: capture the authorised payment
post.description: After the diner confirms the intent. Checks again, then captures or releases the hold; shared with the webhook and the sweep, so the answer is right when one of them already finished the payment. A payment still processing is recorded pending (202). When the outcome can't be told yet the answer is 502 with `reason: "STILL_CONFIRMING"`: don't pay again; the cart updates once it's known, and the diner gets a notice. Not rate limited: a refused capture would leave an authorised payment unfinished.

get.description: Public: anyone at the table (no sign-in) sees the table's order, with its table-wide notices. A signed-in diner also gets the notices meant for them, their card payments' outcomes among them. With no open cart, the 404 carries the notices a signed-in diner who took part in a cart closed lately would otherwise miss. A cookie that is present but expired or invalid is a 401, so the front end refreshes it rather than show a guest view.

post.summary: Stripe's events
post.description: Called by Stripe, not by clients: trusted by the `Stripe-Signature` header over the body's exact bytes (the signing secret is `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). The endpoint subscribes to `payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated`, `payment_intent.succeeded`, `payment_intent.payment_failed`, `payment_intent.canceled` and `refund.failed`; other types are answered 200 and ignored. Handlers are idempotent and act on the state they find, since Stripe may repeat or reorder events. A 500 asks Stripe to retry (for up to 3 days); the server's 2-minute sweep is the backstop either way.

400.description: "Invalid Stripe signature": no raw body, no header, or a signature that doesn't verify

500.description: "Stripe event … not handled yet: retry it"; or "Generic Server Error" (Stripe retries both)

get.description: Always 200 while the process answers; says which version runs and for how long. For the host's health check and a quick look after a deploy.
